review_note: Concise original summaries of cited reference facts. No protected prose or illustrations copied. Field verification and owner/expert review are not claimed.

traits.left: Larger, roughly crow-sized (37–51 cm long); larger head and chest.
traits.right: Smaller, roughly jay-sized (23–34 cm long); smaller head and body.

traits.left: Blocky head, broad chest and rounded tail tip.
traits.right: Small rounded head, narrow body and squared tail tip.

traits.left: Adult cap is darker than the back; juveniles are streaked below. Sex and age are not inferred here.
traits.right: Adult hood and back are similar in tone; juveniles are streaked below. Sex and age are not inferred here.

traits.left: Accipiter flight with slower wingbeats and glides.
traits.right: Fast, choppy wingbeats with flap-glide sequences.

traits.left: Woodlands, forest edges, suburbs and open wooded areas.
traits.right: Forests and woodland edges; often more retiring.

traits.left: Reference accounts describe kik/kak series; use the accepted recordings for actual examples.
traits.right: Reference accounts describe higher, rapid kik notes; differences can be subtle.

gaps: Do not infer sex, age or plumage class from unlabelled accepted media.

traits.left: Smaller, roughly sparrow-sized (14–18 cm long).
traits.right: Larger, roughly robin-sized (18–26 cm long).

traits.left: Short bill, about one-third to one-half the head length.
traits.right: Long, chisel-like bill, nearly the length of the head.

traits.left: Outer tail feathers usually show black spots; source annotations are not interpreted as verified traits.
traits.right: Outer tail feathers usually unmarked white; source annotations are not interpreted as verified traits.

traits.left: Forages on small branches, weeds and trunks; active and often tame.
traits.right: Forages on larger trunks and branches; stronger excavator.

traits.left: Woodlands, orchards, parks and suburbs.
traits.right: Mature forests, woodlots and wooded suburbs.

traits.left: Reference accounts describe a short pik call and a descending whinny.
traits.right: Reference accounts describe a louder peek call and a rattling call.

gaps: The comparison does not assign age, sex or plumage labels to individual accepted photos.

traits.left: Larger (64–81 cm long) with a longer tail.
traits.right: Smaller (60–68 cm long) with a shorter, square tail.

traits.left: Long, rounded tail and long wings; small head.
traits.right: Short, square tail and broad wings; compact body.

traits.left: Two-toned underwing: dark leading edge and silvery trailing flight feathers.
traits.right: Blackish body and wings with silvery-white wingtips.

traits.left: Soars with wings held in a shallow dihedral and often rocks; rarely flaps.
traits.right: Soars with flatter wings and more frequent flapping.

traits.left: Open country, roadsides, forests and farmland.
traits.right: Open country, towns and roadsides; often social.

traits.left: Usually silent; reference accounts describe soft hisses and grunts.
traits.right: Usually silent; reference accounts describe soft hisses.

gaps: Head-color descriptions are not applied to an individual unless the accepted image supports it.

traits.left: Larger (27–30 cm long) with a longer bill.
traits.right: Smaller (23–27 cm long) with a shorter bill.

traits.left: Long bill often slightly upturned; long legs and neck.
traits.right: Shorter, straight bill; compact body and shorter neck.

traits.left: Mottled gray-brown above and pale below; similar to Lesser.
traits.right: Mottled gray-brown above and pale below; similar to Greater.

traits.left: Forages actively in shallow water; often gives a three-note call.
traits.right: Forages in shallow water; often gives a two-note call.

traits.left: Mudflats, marshes, ponds and wet fields.
traits.right: Mudflats, marshes, ponds and wet fields.

traits.left: Reference accounts describe a ringing three-note call.
traits.right: Reference accounts describe a shorter two-note call.

gaps: Separating silent birds in similar plumage requires care; use multiple media examples and source references.
